records.label: spacr.qt.mask_engine.secondary_object_instances#1
records.source: Every positive primary label is a marker, including all its pixels. Intensity growth follows the negative, optionally Gaussian-smoothed image. records.translation: Cada etiqueta primaria positiva es un marcador, incluidos todos sus píxeles. El crecimiento por intensidad sigue la imagen en negativo, opcionalmente suavizada con una gaussiana. El crecimiento por distancia inunda una superficie plana desde los píxeles primarios. Los umbrales de parada comunes restringen los caminos de conectividad a cuatro vecinos alrededor de los píxeles excluidos; seed_fraction recorta después del crecimiento. Esto no es una asignación sin restricciones al primario euclidiano más cercano. Ninguno de los dos modos es el algoritmo de propagación distancia/intensidad (Propagation) de CellProfiler.

And it carries no phenotype images, because the phenotype phase aligns anchors spread over the whole well, which a two-microscope field of view sample cannot supply.

Y no lleva imágenes de fenotipo, porque la fase de fenotipo alinea anclajes repartidos por todo el pocillo, que una muestra de dos campos no puede aportar.

records.label: spacr.qt.preferences.apply_night_theme#4
records.source: AND IT NEVER SWITCHES THE BACKDROP BACK ON. "No animation" is stored as the animation NAME (:data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), which :func:`get_ambient_enabled` reads, so writing an animation over it would hand a moving backdrop to a user who had turned motion off -- through the Animation control, or through Extra Performance, which turns it off the same way. :func:`backdrop_is_switched_off` is therefore asked first, and when it says yes the two ambient keys are left exactly as they are. The theme still changes the colours and the sound set; it just does not start anything moving. What that costs is small and worth saying: a user who later switches the backdrop on gets the animation they had before, not the one this theme would have brought, and they can pick it on the same control they just used.

records.translation: Y NUNCA VUELVE A ACTIVAR EL FONDO. "No animation" se guarda como el NOMBRE de la animación (:data:`spacr.qt.widgets.ambient.NO_ANIMATION`), que lee :func:`get_ambient_enabled`, así que escribir una animación encima daría un fondo en movimiento a un usuario que había desactivado el movimiento -- mediante el control Animación, o mediante Extra Performance, que lo desactiva de la misma forma. records.label: spacr.qt.preferences.resolve_effective_theme#1
records.source: Resolves an explicitly chosen ``"system"`` to the operating system's colour scheme as Qt reports it (``QStyleHints.colorScheme``), and to dark when Qt can't tell. It does not read the application palette: that is spaCR's own once a theme has been applied, so it would answer with whatever was applied last. Every other value passes through, so callers that only understand light/dark should compare against ``"light"`` and treat everything else as dark (Space and Cell are dark themes).
records.context: Resolves an explicitly chosen ``"system"`` to the operating system's colour scheme as Qt reports it (``QStyleHints.colorScheme``), and to dark when Qt can't tell. It does not read the application palette: that is spaCR's own once a theme has been applied, so it would answer with whatever was applied last. Every other value passes through, so callers that only understand light/dark should compare against ``"light"`` and treat everything else as dark (Space and Cell are dark themes).
records.translation: Resuelve un ``"system"`` elegido explícitamente al esquema de color del sistema operativo tal como lo indica Qt (``QStyleHints.colorScheme``), y a oscuro cuando Qt no lo sabe. Cualquier otro valor se pasa tal cual, así que quien solo entienda claro/oscuro debe comparar con ``"light"`` y tratar todo lo demás como oscuro (Space y Cell son temas oscuros).
